title.value: Characterizing the Interpersonal Neural Dynamics of Real-World Social Interactions: Evidence From Classrooms and Museums
title.justification: The title 'Characterizing the Interpersonal Neural Dynamics of Real-World Social Interactions: Evidence From Classrooms and Museums' clearly reflects the paper's focus on studying neural interactions in real-world settings.
title.quote: Characterizing the Interpersonal Neural Dynamics of Real-World Social Interactions: Evidence From Classrooms and Museums

analysis.description: This paper explores the study of neural dynamics during real-world social interactions, using EEG technology to record data in naturalistic settings such as classrooms and museums. It emphasizes the importance of validating laboratory findings in real-world contexts and utilizes interdisciplinary crowdsourcing methods to gather data.

type.justification: The paper discusses real-world studies conducted with EEG technology to gather empirical evidence on neural interactions during social interactions.
type.quote: In a series of real-world neuroscience studies conducted in educational and artistic contexts, we use low-cost portable electroencephalogram (EEG) technology to record neural data.

name.justification: The paper is focused on understanding the neural basis of social interactions, which falls directly under the field of Social Neuroscience.
name.quote: Over the course of the past two decades, laboratory neuroscience has generated valuable insights into the human social brain, but very few social neuroscience studies to date have been conducted in real-world social contexts.

name.justification: The paper employs EEG technology for hyperscanning in real-world social contexts, suggesting its relevance as a sub-field.
name.quote: In a series of real-world neuroscience studies conducted in educational and artistic contexts, we use low-cost portable electroencephalogram (EEG) technology to record neural data from groups of 4-15 people and dyads during naturalistic face-to-face interactions.
